rule: Every event here is a clock with a random draw inside it. Window bosses use a pure function of time (base, period, start and end offsets) and one random moment inside the window. The aura event rolls an hour's random moment, broadcasts a warning, waits 2 to 5 minutes, rolls a count of 1 to 3, and spawns each boss near one randomly chosen eligible player behind a short placeholder. The Ultimate Battle arena runs a five-minute warning, a ten-second countdown, then four rounds separated by data-driven waits. Castle wars repeat on an interval, open with a clean-up and end with a clean-up and a reset. Defects in the donor: the window search steps one period at a time; the spawn moment is redrawn on every call; the aura controller dies on one exception; the Crack of Time mixes milliseconds and ticks; the arena keeps waiting with no members.

warning broadcast, short walk, then the spawn (aura event)

daily cap per connection, moved to per-account and per-device in ours (aura event)

five-minute warning and ten-second countdown with a start line (arena)

change: D1: window search steps one period at a time; replace with closed form
D2: spawn moment redrawn on every call; draw once per cycle and store
D3: no base date means server start; use an explicit anchor in data
D4: one exception ends the aura controller for the uptime; catch per cycle
D5: Crack of Time mixes ms and ticks (window about 198 days as written); use ms from a clock
D6: aura pick uses a snapshot taken before a 2 to 5 minute wait; re-check online state and connection at pick time
D7: arena keeps waiting with zero members; end when empty
per-IP cap replaced by per-account and per-device caps
boss list is zone data, not a config string
walk time shortened for phone play (ours 60 to 120 s)
all times in one unit read from the server clock
look_test: Style flag on the existing fight scene, published to the preview folder, no release rows. Flag A: a red banner 'a strange aura has appeared' with a 60 s countdown chip, then a three-second placeholder ring under one spot a few tiles from the player, then one boss; compare with a plain spawn at the same spot. Flag B: a ten-second countdown card with a large number and a start card, then two rounds with a 20 s gap; compare with no countdown. Judge at 375 wide: banner readable in one glance, ring reads in three seconds, countdown feels like an event not a delay.
